statutoryAuthority.ruleStatement: Upon the discharge and dismissal of a person pursuant to SDCL § 23A-27-14, a court shall order that all official records, other than the nonpublic records retained by the Division of Criminal Investigation, be sealed along with all records relating to the arrest, indictment or information, trial, finding of guilt, and dismissal and discharge. The order restores the person to the status occupied before arrest, indictment or information, and the person is not guilty of perjury or of giving a false statement for failing to recite or acknowledge the matter. Sealing is the court's mandatory duty; there is no ordinary participant motion that triggers the initial sealing. The decided product for the recorded failure branch is: expected sealing at discharge and dismissal, verify court access status, a written implementation request in the original case attaching the discharge and dismissal order and asking the clerk or sentencing judge to enter and implement the statutorily required sealing order, a motion in the original criminal docket to enforce § 23A-27-17 if not corrected, and attorney handoff for refusal or mandamus.
doNotImport: Do not use a form designed for the separate arrest-expungement statute as a fallback; the decision forbids it.
Do not ask for sealing before the discharge and dismissal has issued; the statute does not yet direct it.
Do not draft the sealing order itself; the statute makes it the court's order to enter.

Do not say sealing removes every government record for every purpose; the nonpublic records retained by the Division of Criminal Investigation are expressly outside the order and remain available to law enforcement, prosecutors and courts for future sentencing, future SIS eligibility and habitual-offender determinations.
Do not invent a filing fee, a delivery method or a copy count; no committed record this family binds establishes any of them.
Do not decide whether the case was eligible for the suspended imposition of sentence in the first place; an eligibility dispute is a recorded attorney handoff.

Do not tell a certified-teacher licence holder or applicant convicted under the specified subdivisions of § 22-22-1 or under § 22-22-7 that the seal protects the licence; the licensure authority may refuse or revoke notwithstanding §§ 23A-27-14 and 23A-27-17.

finalVerificationRequirements: Confirm from the court's own orders that the court conditions were completed and that the order discharging the participant and dismissing the case issued; if it has not, nothing in this packet applies.

Obtain the suspended imposition of sentence order and the order of discharge and dismissal from the office of the court in the original criminal case, and copy the court, county, case number and discharge date from them.
Keep a dated copy of the public record search that still shows the matter, and describe it on the request in the participant's own words.

File the written implementation request first, in the original case, with the discharge and dismissal order attached; file the enforcement motion in the original criminal docket only if the record is not corrected.
Ask the office of the court in the original criminal case whether a filing fee applies and how it accepts delivery; neither is established by the committed records.
The participant signs and dates each page personally; the sealing order itself is the court's and is never drafted.

hearingAndObjectionStops.situation: The discharge and dismissal has not issued, the court conditions are not complete, or the discharge status is unclear.
hearingAndObjectionStops.whatItMeans: The sealing duty has not been triggered and nothing in this packet applies.

hearingAndObjectionStops.situation: The court refuses after the enforcement motion.
hearingAndObjectionStops.whatItMeans: The recorded escalation is attorney handoff for refusal or mandamus, a lawyer's work rather than another filing from this packet.

hearingAndObjectionStops.situation: Eligibility for the suspended imposition of sentence is disputed in any way, or the matter is a felony matter.
hearingAndObjectionStops.whatItMeans: An eligibility dispute is a recorded attorney handoff and any felony matter is outside self-help.

hearingAndObjectionStops.situation: The underlying conviction was under the specified subdivisions of SDCL § 22-22-1 or under § 22-22-7 and the participant holds or seeks a South Dakota certified teaching licence.
hearingAndObjectionStops.whatItMeans: The licensure authority may refuse or revoke notwithstanding the sealing; the participant gets advice before relying on the seal.

hearingAndObjectionStops.situation: The participant is relying on sealing to erase the matter everywhere.
hearingAndObjectionStops.whatItMeans: The Division of Criminal Investigation's nonpublic records are expressly outside the order.

hearingAndObjectionStops.situation: Any immigration question is involved, or the records are federal, tribal, military or out-of-state.
hearingAndObjectionStops.whatItMeans: Both are outside the approved self-help boundary.

participantChecklist.text: Confirm that your court conditions were completed and that the order of discharge and dismissal issued; if it has not, stop, because nothing here applies.
Get the SIS order and the discharge and dismissal order from the office of the court in the original criminal case, and copy the court, county, case number and discharge date from them.

Fill in and file the written request in the original case, attaching the discharge and dismissal order and dated evidence that the matter still appears on a public record search, after asking that court's office how it accepts delivery.
File the enforcement motion in the original criminal docket only if the record is not corrected after the written request.

Sign and date each page yourself, and know that sealing restores your pre-arrest status and protects you from perjury for not acknowledging the matter, but does not reach the Division of Criminal Investigation's nonpublic records.
